newsitem.title: USA: Navistar sees lower heavy truck demand.
newsitem.headline: Navistar sees lower heavy truck demand.

text.p: Navistar International Corp said Thursday it expects industry demand for heavy trucks in the United States and Canada will reach 170,000 units in 1997, down 13 percent from 195,400 heavy trucks sold by the industry in 1996.
"While we have not revised our forecast, current order receipts indicate that there may be some strength beyond this level," John Horne, chairman, said in a statement.
The company also expects industry demand for medium trucks in the United States and Canada will reach 112,000 units in 1997, a slight decrease from 113,200 trucks in 1996.
Navistar said it expects industry demand for school buses in fiscal 1997 to remain relatively flat year over year with the 32,500 buses sold in 1996.

Earlier, Navistar reported income for the fiscal first quarter ended January 31 of $0.10 a share, down from $0.20 a year ago. Total sales and revenues for the quarter declined to $1.3 billion from $1.43 billion.
Navistar said its worldwide shipments of 20,400 medium and heavy trucks and school buses during the first quarter were 15.9 percent lower than a year ago.

"Demand for trucks is fairly strong by historical standards. In fact, our order receipts in the first quarter are up across the board in school buses and medium and heavy trucks compared with 1996," Horne said.
Due to increased demand for trucks, Navistar said it plans to boost production at its Springfield, Ohio truck assembly plant in the upcoming quarter.

Production on the plant's medium truck and school bus line will increase from 224 to 266 units per day, with heavy truck production growing from 47 to 65 trucks per day. In line with those plans, Navistar said it intends to call back 500 employees in February.
"On the engine side, we continue to see strong demand due to our ability to deliver efficiencies and improvements in first-time quality," Horne said.

Shipments of mid-range diesel engines to other original equipment manufacturers during the fiscal first quarter totaled 41,000 units, an 8.4 percent increase over last year. Sales of parts were $186 million, compared to $177 million in the same period a year ago, an increase of 5.1 percent.
On a quarter-to-quarter comparison, the gross margin rose to 13.6 percent in 1997 from 12.2 percent, Navistar said.
